surfaces.part: rock mound upper lit facets (top planes)

answer.evidence: The rock pile's silhouette widens gradually from 12px at row 5 to 44px by row 17, so it has a sloped, lit upper mass. In column x=13 the light facets (white at rows 7-11, L=196 at rows 13-17) end in a darker edge line at row 18 (L=152). Row 19 is darker (L=125), and a darker front face follows to row 29, so the top planes are followed by an edge line, shadow and a vertical front. Column x=34 shows the same pattern: light rows 15-20, edge line at row 21, shadow at row 22, then darker front rows 23-28. The top-to-front structure is irregular, as expected for a natural rock, but it reads as a top surface plus a front face of 3+ rows.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a grey rock outcrop, not a tree, bush or plant. It has no canopy or trunk, so the references do not match its kind. It also reads as a small, sparse object next to the full trees. The rock body has about 4 grey steps (white highlight patch, light, mid, dark). The measured dark edge pixels are 100% near-neutral, so the outline is a neutral dark line rather than a tinted material tone. This is the sticker look the standard rejects. Visible tones per tile (11) are above tree-1a786c (7) but well below tree-d43edd (29). Flat coverage is 12% against 0% for both references, and the white highlight patches are flat fills. Stones are shaded as large blocks, not one by one, and the grain is thin. Overall it is shallower than the references: neutral outline, some flat areas, and fewer steps.
